missing_aspects: IM-MS features for model training are weakly covered: exact charge-state distributions, collision cross section (CCS) values across conformers, arrival-time distributions/peak widths, gas-phase unfolding transitions as a function of activation energy, and metal-bound vs apo conformer ratios for each zinc finger variant.

Validation of structural integrity after computational design is weakly covered: orthogonal confirmation of proper Cys2-His2 folding and Zn2+ coordination by circular dichroism, NMR/X-ray/HDX-MS, and IM-MS reproducibility across independent preparations.

Validation of improved drug-like properties is weakly covered: direct PK/ADME readouts such as serum stability, plasma protein binding, microsomal/hepatocyte stability, clearance, half-life, permeability, and aggregation/solubility assays for the predicted variants.

refinement_metadata.query: zinc finger protein ion mobility mass spectrometry collision cross section metal binding tertiary fold deep learning pharmacokinetic properties structural stability ADME variant design
missing_aspects: IM-MS metrics not yet well specified for model training: collision cross section (CCS) distributions, arrival time drift profiles, charge-state distribution, oligomeric/compactness shifts upon zinc binding, and metal-bound vs apo conformer abundances/stability across collision energy.

Validation workflow for predicted variants is undercovered: orthogonal structural confirmation of correct zinc-coordinated folding after mutation, direct comparison of wild-type and variant IM-MS profiles, and independent assays for DNA-binding activity plus drug-property readouts such as protease stability, serum stability, solubility, aggregation, and plasma half-life/PK.

No strong evidence yet on coupling IM-MS-derived conformational features with deep learning to predict how sequence modifications alter pharmacokinetic/ developability properties while preserving zinc finger tertiary integrity.
